points: Q3 2026 results will show whether DFIN can sustain the 2.8% year-over-year revenue growth reported for Q2, or if demand for regulatory software is accelerating.

The 90-day revenue estimate is up 2.70% and analysts have revised estimates 2 up versus 0 down over the past 30 days; the print will test whether that estimate momentum is backed by actual Q3 performance.
Consensus looks for FY1 EPS of $4.82 and FY2 EPS of $5.46, implying growth slows from about 53% to 13%; Q3 guidance and commentary will reveal whether FY2 can hold that trajectory or re-accelerate.
DFIN trades at a deep discount to the theme on P/E and PEG, so the Q3 print needs to confirm the earnings path behind the FY1/FY2 estimates to support a rerating.
Reports suggest software momentum and regulatory shifts were key drivers in Q2; the Q3 call should update whether those trends continued through the summer and into the 2027 pipeline.
Peer prints from CBOE, ICE, MSCI and VIRT within days of DFIN will offer a cross-check on market-activity and data-demand conditions that could affect DFIN's forward-quarter setup.
watch: Q3 revenue growth at or above the Q2 2.8% year-over-year pace supports the long.
FY2 EPS estimate staying near $5.46 or moving higher supports the long.
PEG staying at or below about 0.3x the theme median supports the long valuation case.
Analyst revision count staying positive (more up than down over 30 days) supports the long.
